title: A magnet sits inside a coil
hook: A strong magnet rests inside a coil of wire. Is it making electricity right now?

knows: magnets and coils can make electricity (generators, bike dynamos)
a meter shows current or voltage
doesNotKnow: Faraday's law: the voltage depends on how fast the magnetic flux through the coil changes
Lenz's law: moving in and moving out push the current opposite ways

misconception: A strong magnet inside a coil produces a current just by being there.
objective: The learner can explain that a coil responds only to a change in the magnetic flux through it, so a magnet held still inside gives exactly zero, and pushing in and pulling out give kicks of opposite sign.

claims.text: A coil's voltage is set by how fast the magnetic flux through it changes: voltage = number of turns × rate of change of flux (Faraday's law).
claims.source: Faraday's law of induction, emf = -N dPhi/dt (OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2, section 13.1 Faraday's Law).

claims.text: A magnet held still inside the coil gives a steady flux, so the meter reads zero, however strong the magnet.
claims.source: dPhi/dt = 0 for a stationary magnet and coil, so emf = 0 exactly (artifacts/scratch/w4phys/check.mjs). Ideal coil and meter; ignores the Earth's field, which is also steady.

claims.text: Pushing the magnet in and pulling it out make the needle kick in opposite directions.
claims.source: Lenz's law: the induced emf opposes the change in flux; increasing and decreasing flux give opposite signs (OpenStax University Physics Vol. 2, section 13.2 Lenz's Law). In the model the two moves are mirror images in time, giving +/- the same peak.

claims.text: In this illustrative set-up (100 turns, 0.1 mWb through the coil with the magnet inside, 0.3 s moves) each push or pull peaks at about 123 mV.
claims.source: Flux model Phi(z) = 0.1 mWb / (1 + (z / 2 cm)^2)^1.5 (on-axis dipole through a short coil of radius 2 cm), z from -8 cm to 0 by smoothstep over 0.3 s; numerical differentiation (dt = 1e-5 s) in artifacts/scratch/w4phys/check.mjs: peak 0.1234 V at 0.226 s; the pulse's integral equals N x change of flux, 9.86 mV s. Parameters are illustrative, not a measured magnet.

claims.text: The coil, magnet and meter values are illustrative; the zero while the magnet is still is not.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('Illustrative coil') and in the reveal. The zero follows from c2 for any magnet and coil.

recall.question: A bike dynamo has a magnet that spins inside a coil. When the bike stops, with the magnet still inside the coil, the dynamo's output is…
recall.why: A coil only produces a voltage while the magnetic flux through it is changing. A magnet that has stopped gives a steady flux, so no voltage.
